summary:
**Planetary Analog Mission Control – Terrestrial Analog Matching Engine**

Planetary Analog Mission Control is an interactive planetary exploration platform powered by a Terrestrial Analog Matching Engine, designed to identify Earth environments that exhibit characteristics comparable to Mars, the Moon, and Venus.

By combining adjustable environmental parameters, a comparative matching algorithm, interactive geospatial mapping, and visual analytics, the platform enables users to explore potential terrestrial analog sites and investigate how Earth's extreme environments can help us understand other worlds.

Users can select a planetary target, modify environmental conditions, and explore candidate locations such as the Atacama Desert, Mojave Desert, and McMurdo Dry Valleys. The system generates comparative match scores and highlights promising locations for further investigation.

This project makes planetary analog exploration more accessible, engaging, and understandable. It creates a bridge between Earth-based environmental exploration and planetary science, inspiring scientific curiosity and supporting future research, education, and exploration. Our vision is to transform Earth's most extreme landscapes into stepping stones toward understanding worlds beyond our own.

**One Earth. Many Worlds. Infinite Possibilities.**
details:
Planetary Analog Mission Control – Terrestrial Analog Matching Engine

1. Project Overview: Exploring Other Worlds Through Earth

Planetary Analog Mission Control is an interactive planetary exploration platform powered by a Terrestrial Analog Matching Engine. It aims to identify Earth locations with environmental characteristics comparable to Mars, the Moon, and Venus.

From hyper-arid deserts and volcanic regions to frozen polar landscapes and salt flats, Earth's extreme environments offer valuable opportunities to investigate conditions and geological processes found on other worlds.

Our platform connects planetary science, environmental comparison, geospatial exploration, and interactive technology.

2. What Does the Project Do?

The platform enables users to explore potential terrestrial analog locations through environmental comparisons.

Users can select a planetary target, adjust eight environmental parameters, explore nine candidate locations worldwide, generate comparative matching scores, and visualize locations through interactive maps.

The eight parameters include humidity, wind speed, atmospheric pressure, radiation, surface roughness, iron oxide mineralogy, permafrost depth, and thermal inertia.

3. How Does It Work?

The Terrestrial Analog Matching Engine compares selected environmental settings with stored candidate-site values.

The current prototype evaluates three parameters: humidity, radiation, and surface roughness, applying weighted differences to generate exploratory matching scores.

Penalty = (0.40 × Humidity Difference) + (0.05 × Radiation Difference) + (10 × Surface Roughness Difference)

Match Score = Clamp (99.6 − Penalty, 78.0, 99.6)

Interactive geographical markers and location information help users investigate potential analog environments. These scores are prototype heuristic outputs, not scientifically validated measures of planetary similarity.

4. How Was the Project Created?

We developed this browser-based application using:

  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: Core application and functionality.
  • Tailwind CSS: Interface design and styling.
  • Three.js: Space-inspired animated introduction.
  • Leaflet.js: Interactive geographical mapping.
  • Chart.js: Visual environmental analytics.
  • OpenStreetMap and Esri World Imagery: Geographical and satellite-map layers.

A separate 3D Mars model is also included in our project materials.

5. What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

Our development considered environmental diversity, planetary relevance, geographical accessibility, scientific interpretability, and user experience.

We selected diverse extreme environments and designed an intuitive interface to make planetary comparisons accessible. We also recognize the importance of reliable datasets, consistent measurements, justified scoring weights, uncertainty estimates, and scientific validation.

6. Intended Benefits and Global Impact

Our project aims to connect Earth observation with planetary exploration.

  • Planetary science: Provides an exploratory framework for comparing terrestrial and planetary characteristics.
  • Education: Makes planetary science more interactive and accessible to students and educators.
  • Research: Offers a starting point for identifying potential terrestrial analog environments.
  • Scientific awareness: Highlights the importance of Earth's extreme landscapes in understanding other worlds.
  • Future exploration: Could support preliminary research planning through validated datasets and improved scientific models.

7. Future Development and Vision

We aim to evolve the prototype into a scientifically grounded planetary analog intelligence platform by integrating authoritative NASA and other scientific datasets, expanding the matching algorithm, introducing target-specific reference conditions, improving scoring calibration, and incorporating uncertainty estimates and scientific validation.

Future enhancements also include an expanded geographical database, improved 3D visualization, and detailed environmental comparison reports.

8. Our Mission: One Earth, Many Worlds

Planetary Analog Mission Control represents our belief that understanding other worlds begins with understanding our own.

From the iron-rich deserts of Chile to the frozen landscapes of Antarctica, Earth's extreme environments offer extraordinary opportunities to investigate planetary geology, environmental processes, and the future of exploration.

Through this project, our team aims to combine scientific curiosity, technological creativity, and an ambitious spirit of discovery.

We are not simply mapping extreme places on Earth. We are building a starting point for exploring how our planet can help us understand others.

One Earth. Many Worlds. Infinite Possibilities.
